es.summary: Prueba de tamizaje del cáncer de cérvix: se toman células del cuello uterino y se revisan al microscopio para detectar cambios anormales antes de que se vuelvan cáncer.
key_points: Detecta células precancerosas (displasia) y, a veces, infecciones o inflamación.
Casi todos los cánceres de cérvix se deben a infecciones persistentes por VPH de alto riesgo; la muestra también puede analizarse para VPH.
Un resultado anormal no significa cáncer: el PAP no diagnostica cáncer, se confirma con colposcopía y biopsia.
La frecuencia depende de la edad y de los resultados previos; seguir la norma nacional y la indicación médica.
Se puede tomar durante el embarazo.

normal_values: Normal o «negativo»: sin cambios anormales en las células del cérvix.
Insatisfactorio: la muestra no tuvo suficientes células; se repite.
Anormal o «positivo»: cambios celulares que requieren seguimiento (por ejemplo colposcopía).
specimen: Con espéculo, se toman células del cérvix con un cepillo o espátula y se envían al laboratorio.
No tomarlo durante la menstruación; idealmente unos 5 días después de terminar la regla.
Dos días antes, evitar tampones, cremas u óvulos vaginales, duchas vaginales y relaciones sexuales vaginales.
nursing_care: Explicar el procedimiento: puede causar molestia leve, presión o un sangrado muy leve.
Preguntar la FUR, embarazo y uso de DIU antes de tomar la muestra.
Anotar la fecha y el resultado del último PAP en los AGO.
Asegurar que la paciente reciba y entienda el resultado y su seguimiento.

en.summary: A screening test for cervical cancer: cells are collected from the cervix and checked under a microscope for abnormal changes before they become cancer.
key_points: A Pap smear looks for abnormal changes in cervical cells before they become cancer, and may also find certain infections or inflammation.
Long-lasting infections with high-risk types of HPV cause almost all cervical cancers; the cells can also be checked for HPV.
Most of the time, abnormal results do not mean you have cervical cancer: a Pap smear doesn't diagnose cancer, which is confirmed by colposcopy and biopsy.
How often it is needed depends on age and previous results; follow national guidelines and the provider's order.
It can be done during pregnancy.

normal_values: Normal or "negative" result: no abnormal changes were found in the cervix cells.
Unsatisfactory: the lab sample did not have enough cells; the test is repeated.
Abnormal or "positive" result: abnormal changes were found in the cervical cells and need follow-up (for example colposcopy).
specimen: Using a speculum, the provider collects cells from the cervix with a small brush or swab and sends them to a lab.
You should not have a Pap smear while you are having your period; a good time is about five days after the last day of your period.
For two days before the test, avoid tampons, vaginal creams or medicines, douching and vaginal sex.
nursing_care: Explain the procedure: there may be mild discomfort, pressure or very light bleeding afterward.
Ask about the LMP, pregnancy and IUD use before collecting the sample.
Record the date and result of the last Pap test in the OB/GYN history (AGO).
Make sure the patient receives and understands the result and the follow-up plan.

summary.0.quote: A Pap smear looks for abnormal changes in cervical cells before they become cancer.

key_points.0.quote: A pap smear may also find certain infections or inflammation.

sections.normal_values.0.quote: Normal or "negative" result , which usually means that no abnormal changes were found in your cervix cells.

sections.normal_values.1.quote: Unsatisfactory results , which may mean that the lab sample did not have enough cells, or the cells may have been clumped together or hidden by mucus.

sections.normal_values.2.quote: Abnormal or "positive" result , which usually means that abnormal changes were found in your cervical cells.

sections.specimen.1.quote: You should not have a Pap smear while you are having your period because this may affect your results.

sections.specimen.2.quote: For two days before your test, you should not: Use tampons Use birth control foam, jelly, or cream Use other creams or medicines in your vagina Douche (rinse the vagina with water or other fluid) Have vaginal sex

sections.nursing_care.0.quote: You may feel some mild discomfort during a Pap smear and have some very light bleeding afterward, but there are no known risks to having a Pap smear.
